title: Add AWS Step Functions orchestrator example for RAG pipelines (CDK + Express StepFn)
author: Maya Patel
body:
Motivation: provide a reference implementation for teams that want to run multi-stage Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) workflows at scale using AWS Step Functions (Express) orchestrator backed by CDK. Many customers ask how to compose retrieval, chunking, model calls, and external tool invocation with deterministic retries, observability, and low orchestration cost — this example demonstrates a pragmatic pattern using a lightweight state machine and Redwood SDK calls from Lambda tasks.

What this PR contains: a self-contained examples/rag-stepfn-cdk/ directory with: CDK app (TypeScript) that provisions an Express Step Function, Lambda task handlers (Node.js) that call Redwood via the SDK for retrieval and generation steps, a small DynamoDB-backed vector cache example, an EventBridge + WebSocket stub for streaming partial outputs back to a dev client, sample IAM least-privilege policies, and a README with local dev and deploy instructions. The example favors clarity and ops-readiness over production hardening; we document trade-offs.

Key design decisions and trade-offs: single-step model invocation is wrapped in a Lambda to keep StepFn debugability and retries simple; long-running model streaming is simulated with short-lived step functions + EventBridge because Express StepFn has 5-minute limits — we call out options (Activity workers, SQS+Fargate) for production. We show how to pin model versions and configure fallback model routing (via environment variables) to mirror Redwood routing policies.

Local dev quickstart (excerpt):
  1) yarn install && cd examples/rag-stepfn-cdk && yarn bootstrap
  2) cp .env.example .env and set REDWOOD_API_KEY, AWS creds, and LOCAL_VECTOR_DIR
  3) yarn start:local (runs SAM local for Lambdas + StepFn local runner shim)
  4) curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/start -d '{"query":"What is Redwood Inference?"}' to exercise the pipeline

Included files (high level): examples/rag-stepfn-cdk/README.md, examples/rag-stepfn-cdk/cdk/bin/app.ts, examples/rag-stepfn-cdk/cdk/lib/stepfn-stack.ts, examples/rag-stepfn-cdk/lambdas/retriever/index.ts, examples/rag-stepfn-cdk/lambdas/generator/index.ts, examples/rag-stepfn-cdk/lambdas/stream-proxy/index.ts, examples/rag-stepfn-cdk/templates/stepfn-definition.json, examples/rag-stepfn-cdk/test/integration.sh

Testing notes: unit tests added for the Lambda handlers (jest) and a lightweight integration script that runs against local SAM. CI is configured to run the TypeScript build, lint, and unit tests in the repository examples job. We intentionally do not run full CDK deploys in CI to avoid creating infra in CI, but CDK synth is executed for smoke validation.

Security and least-privilege: example IAM policies are scoped to the example resources and documented in README. We surface common hardening recommendations (KMS for secrets, private VPC endpoints for DynamoDB, restrict StepFn execution role to specific ARNs).

Docs and dev experience: README contains architecture diagram (ASCII), sequence of traceable event IDs for tracing, and a troubleshooting section with common error messages from the Redwood SDK (auth, rate-limits, model-not-found). We also include a short recipe for switching the Lambda generator to call Redwood Dedicated endpoints (env var REDWOOD_ENDPOINT).

Checklist: 
  - [x] Add CDK stack and minimal IAM
  - [x] Add Lambda handlers and local runner shim
  - [x] Add README with quickstart and architecture notes
  - [x] Add unit tests and CI synth/lint/build steps
  - [x] Add integration smoke script for local manual test

Related work and tracking: references Linear ENG-4123 for multi-step orchestration patterns and DOCS-88 for examples consolidation. This is a self-contained example and does not change Redwood SDK behavior.

Migration notes: this is an additive examples folder; no breaking changes. See release notes below for where to find the example in the docs site tree.

If reviewers prefer a different streaming approach (activities vs EventBridge) I can follow up with an alternate branch and a short doc linking pros/cons.

review_comments: David Kim: nice example — please narrow IAM roles to least privilege and add a short note about cross-account StepFn invocation behavior.
Maya Patel: addressed IAM scoping and added README_SECURITY.md with KMS/VPC recommendations (see commit d4e8b7f).
Olga Sokolov: can we add an example env var to switch to a Dedicated endpoint? also suggest a small paragraph about runtime costs for Express vs Standard StepFns.
Maya Patel: added env var switch and cost paragraph in README; kept Express as default for the quickstart to keep infra small.
Ravi Narayan: approved after verifying local smoke script; left a minor comment about jest timeout which was fixed.
